Preconditions: Branch integration/testing checked out; .env filled from .env.example
Test Case: Server boots with a complete env
Steps: 1. Set DATABASE_URL, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, SESSION_SECRET, ENCRYPTION_KEY (64 hex). 2. Run npm run dev.
Expected Result: Server listens on :5000. No boot error. Client loads at http://localhost:5000/.
Notes: ENCRYPTION_KEY is mandatory - server refuses to boot without it

Test Case: Missing ENCRYPTION_KEY blocks boot
Steps: 1. Unset ENCRYPTION_KEY. 2. Run npm run dev.
Expected Result: Server refuses to boot with an explicit error naming ENCRYPTION_KEY. It does not start with plaintext storage.

Preconditions: Env has OCR_BYPASS, IDENTITY_BYPASS, PAYMENTS_TEST_MODE, OTP_FIXED_CODE set
Test Case: Boot prints a warning box for every active bypass
Steps: 1. Set OCR_BYPASS=1 and PAYMENTS_TEST_MODE=1. 2. Boot the server. 3. Read stdout.
Expected Result: A boxed warning is printed for each active bypass so nobody ships with them on.

Test Case: Migrations apply cleanly on the merged branch
Steps: 1. Apply every file in /migrations in order. 2. Re-run the same set.
Expected Result: All migrations apply. Re-running is order-independent and does not error.
Notes: The merge added no new migrations - the ops-console delta was code only

Test Case: Type check and production build pass
Steps: 1. Run npm run check. 2. Run npm run build.
Expected Result: tsc exits 0 with no output. Build writes dist/public and dist/index.cjs. Only the pre-existing import.meta cjs warning appears.

Test Case: Sessions survive a server restart
Steps: 1. Set REDIS_URL. 2. Log in. 3. Restart the server. 4. Reload the page.
Expected Result: User is still signed in. No forced logout.
Notes: Without REDIS_URL sessions fall back to signed cookies

Test Case: startOfIstDayIso exists exactly once and is correct
Steps: 1. Open shared/istTime.ts. 2. Confirm a single export of startOfIstDayIso. 3. Load the ops dashboard and the agent collections screen.
Expected Result: One definition only. IST day boundaries on the ops board, the transactions ledger and agent collections all resolve to 00:00 +05:30.
Notes: Automerge had produced a duplicate definition; deduped in the merge commit

Test Case: Corporate address and hub state is declared once in Signup.tsx
Steps: 1. Start a company signup. 2. Reach the company details step. 3. Fill address, pincode, city, state and hub.
Expected Result: Each field renders once. Pincode lookup fills city and state. No duplicated address block and no redeclaration error in the console.
Notes: Conflict resolution dropped the duplicate HEAD block

Test Case: Ops board filter hook still drives every board
Steps: 1. Open /ops/pickups, /ops/dropoffs and /ops/dispatched. 2. Apply a filter on each.
Expected Result: All three boards render and filter. No runtime error about a missing import from opsBoardQuery.
Notes: The import block was resolved to the ops-console version

Test Case: POST /api/auth/signup/company still accepts address, pincode, city, state and hub_id
Steps: 1. Submit a company signup with all ITD fields. 2. Inspect the response and the created account.
Expected Result: The account is created. Omitting address, pincode, city, state or hub_id returns 400 with the field-specific message.

Test Case: Guest orders appear on the ops boards alongside account orders
Steps: 1. Book one guest order and one account order. 2. Open /ops/pickups.
Expected Result: Both appear. The guest order shows the guest contact details rather than a blank customer.
Notes: Guest booking is final-phase work and the boards are ops-console work - this is the seam

Preconditions: OTP_FIXED_CODE set to a 6-digit value, or WhatsApp/SMS wired
Test Case: Request a login code
Steps: 1. Open /login. 2. Enter a valid 10-digit Indian mobile. 3. Submit.
Expected Result: The OTP is sent. The UI moves to code entry and says where the code went.

Preconditions: AUTH-001 done; the number belongs to an existing account
Test Case: Sign in with a correct code
Steps: 1. Enter the correct OTP. 2. Submit.
Expected Result: Signed in and redirected to /home. GET /api/auth/me returns the user.

Test Case: Wrong OTP is rejected and locks out after 5 tries
Steps: 1. Enter a wrong 6-digit code five times.
Expected Result: Each attempt errors. After the fifth the code is locked out and a new one must be requested.

Test Case: Expired OTP is rejected
Steps: 1. Request a code. 2. Wait past its TTL. 3. Enter it.
Expected Result: Rejected as expired rather than as wrong. A fresh code can be requested.

Test Case: Malformed phone numbers are refused
Steps: 1. Try an empty number, 9 digits, 11 digits, letters, and a leading +91 form.
Expected Result: Validation blocks submission for each invalid shape. The +91 form is either normalised or clearly rejected - not silently sent.

Test Case: OTP request is rate limited per number
Steps: 1. Request codes for the same number repeatedly in a short window.
Expected Result: The hourly ceiling is enforced and the UI says to wait rather than failing silently.

Test Case: Logout clears the session
Steps: 1. Click logout. 2. Reload. 3. Call GET /api/auth/me.
Expected Result: Signed out and sent to the public surface. /api/auth/me returns 401.

Test Case: An unknown number is routed to signup without a second SMS
Steps: 1. Enter a number with no account at /login. 2. Verify the OTP.
Expected Result: Routed to /signup with the number pre-filled and already verified. No second code is sent.
Notes: Covers 444cdeb - sign in with the code already typed

Test Case: A verifying state is shown while the code is checked
Steps: 1. Submit the OTP on a throttled connection.
Expected Result: A verifying state shows on the button and double submission is prevented.

Preconditions: Phone verified; OCR_BYPASS=1 if there is no VRS production account
Test Case: Open a personal account end to end
Steps: 1. Open /signup and choose personal. 2. Enter name and email. 3. Enter the Aadhaar and PAN numbers. 4. Upload both documents. 5. Sign the contract. 6. Submit.
Expected Result: The account is created, signed in and lands on /home. Documents are stored encrypted.

Test Case: An invalid Aadhaar is refused by the Verhoeff check
Steps: 1. Enter 123456789012. 2. Continue.
Expected Result: Refused as an invalid Aadhaar before any upload.
Notes: shared/aadhaar.ts. Cashfree's canned sandbox Aadhaar starts with 1 and cannot be typed here

Test Case: An invalid PAN shape is refused
Steps: 1. Enter a PAN with the wrong pattern such as 1234ABCDE. 2. Continue.
Expected Result: Refused with a format message. The correct shape ABCDE1234F is accepted.

Preconditions: OCR_BYPASS unset and VRS credentials live
Test Case: A document whose number disagrees with the typed one is refused
Steps: 1. Type a PAN. 2. Upload a document carrying a different PAN.
Expected Result: The upload is rejected as a mismatch and signup cannot proceed on that slot.

Test Case: Bypassed documents are recorded as bypassed, not verified
Steps: 1. Upload any document. 2. Inspect the stored verification status.
Expected Result: Status is bypassed - distinguishable from match, skipped and unreadable.

Test Case: The contract is signed with the typed name stamped on it
Steps: 1. Open the contract preview. 2. Type the signatory name. 3. Accept.
Expected Result: The generated PDF carries the typed name. An empty or invalid signature blocks submission.

Preconditions: Contract viewer open on a small screen
Test Case: The contract viewer close button stays on screen
Steps: 1. Open the contract on a 360px-wide viewport. 2. Scroll.
Expected Result: The close control stays reachable and is not pushed off-canvas.

Preconditions: A phone number that already has an account
Test Case: Signup refuses a number that already has an account
Steps: 1. Start signup with a number that already has an account.
Expected Result: Refused with a message pointing to sign-in, rather than silently signing in or creating a duplicate.

Preconditions: Documents staged mid-signup and the signup abandoned
Test Case: Staged documents are bound to the phone that proved them
Steps: 1. Stage documents against number A. 2. In the same browser verify number B. 3. Try to finish signup.
Expected Result: Documents staged under A are not claimable by B.

Preconditions: WA_CRON_SECRET set and a staged signup older than SIGNUP_RETENTION_DAYS
Test Case: The retention sweep deletes only unclaimed staged documents
Steps: 1. POST /api/admin/retention/sweep with the cron secret.
Expected Result: Documents with a signup_ref older than the window are deleted. Documents belonging to a real account are untouched.

Test Case: The retention sweep rejects an unauthenticated call
Steps: 1. POST /api/admin/retention/sweep with no bearer secret.
Expected Result: Refused. With WA_CRON_SECRET unset the endpoint 404s.

Preconditions: Documents uploaded at the identity step
Test Case: Delete a staged document and re-upload
Steps: 1. Delete the document for a slot from the UI. 2. Upload a replacement.
Expected Result: The slot empties, the replacement is accepted, and the old file is no longer readable.

Preconditions: Cashfree VRS credentials live, or IDENTITY_BYPASS=gstin
Test Case: Open a corporate account end to end
Steps: 1. Open /signup, choose company, category corporate. 2. Enter company name, GSTIN, contact person and email. 3. Enter address, pincode, city, state and hub. 4. Verify the GSTIN. 5. Upload the GST certificate. 6. Sign the contract. 7. Submit.
Expected Result: The account is created and signed in. The ITD fields are persisted with the account.

Test Case: GSTIN must be 15 characters and verify against the portal
Steps: 1. Enter a 14-character GSTIN. 2. Then enter a well-formed but unregistered one.
Expected Result: A length error on the first. A portal lookup failure on the second, blocking the step.

Test Case: A GST certificate that does not carry the verified GSTIN is refused
Steps: 1. Upload a certificate for a different GSTIN.
Expected Result: Refused. The number on the document must match the verified number.

Test Case: A photographed GST certificate falls back to a vision read
Steps: 1. Upload a photo rather than a text-layer PDF of the certificate.
Expected Result: The vision fallback reads it. With OPENAI_API_KEY unset it comes back unverified and blocks the account instead of passing silently.

Test Case: Category-specific export fields are demanded
Steps: 1. Choose e-commerce. 2. Leave lut_no, iec_branch_code, bank_account_no and bank_ad_code blank. 3. Submit.
Expected Result: Blocked with per-field messages. Switching to corporate clears the requirement and stores null rather than stale values.

Test Case: Hub and pincode validation
Steps: 1. Enter a 5-digit pincode. 2. Then a valid one. 3. Leave the hub unselected.
Expected Result: The 5-digit pincode is rejected. A valid pincode auto-fills city and state. A missing hub blocks with Select a hub.

Test Case: A bypassed GSTIN is recorded and disclosed
Steps: 1. Complete a company signup with the bypass on.
Expected Result: identity_verifications records the status as bypassed rather than verified, and the UI tells the customer the number was not checked.

Preconditions: Signed out; a phone number with no account
Test Case: Book a shipment as a guest with no account
Steps: 1. Open /create signed out. 2. Fill the sender details and address. 3. Verify the phone with an OTP. 4. Upload the KYC document asked for. 5. Complete the receiver, parcel and payment steps. 6. Submit.
Expected Result: The order is created against a guest ref. No account is made. The confirmation shows the order number.

Test Case: KYC is asked for after the address, not before
Steps: 1. Walk the sender step from the top.
Expected Result: The address is collected first and the document ask comes after it. No KYC placeholder appears earlier in the step.

Test Case: Verification comes before the corridor card
Steps: 1. Enter the sender step.
Expected Result: Phone verification is requested first. The corridor card is not shown on the sender step.

Preconditions: A phone number that already has an account
Test Case: A number with an account signs in instead of booking as a guest
Steps: 1. At the guest gate enter a number that already has an account. 2. Verify the OTP.
Expected Result: The browser is signed in to that account and the booking continues as an account booking. No guest ref is created.

Test Case: The guest session is bound to the proved number
Steps: 1. Verify number A. 2. Attempt to submit the booking naming number B.
Expected Result: Refused. Documents and the order stay bound to A.

Preconditions: The guest uploaded a KYC document
Test Case: The uploaded document is shown back to the guest
Steps: 1. Upload the document. 2. Stay on the step.
Expected Result: The uploaded file is displayed back with its name or preview rather than an empty control.

Preconditions: A guest order placed with a KYC document
Test Case: The KYC document is claimed by the order rather than orphaned
Steps: 1. Complete a guest booking with a document. 2. Inspect the document row.
Expected Result: The document is linked to the guest ref the order carries. No orphaned row is left behind.
Notes: Covers b14983d. scripts/cleanup-orphaned-guest-kyc.ts exists for pre-existing orphans

Test Case: Creating an account on the same number adopts the guest orders
Steps: 1. After a guest booking on A, sign up on A. 2. Open /orders.
Expected Result: Everything booked as a guest on A now appears under the account and the guest session is cleared.

Test Case: The gate heading is not hardcoded to one destination
Steps: 1. Read the guest gate heading on the sender step.
Expected Result: The heading reflects the selected corridor rather than a fixed destination string.

Test Case: Signup still compels documents - optional KYC is gone
Steps: 1. Start a normal signup. 2. Try to skip a required document.
Expected Result: No skip is offered. The optional-KYC path and its schema columns are gone.
Notes: Covers 0e2b91b, 20df7c5 and the b14983d column purge

Test Case: The rate calculator returns a quote
Steps: 1. Open /rates. 2. Enter the origin pincode, destination, weight and dimensions. 3. Calculate.
Expected Result: A rate is returned with a clear breakdown, and the same inputs give the same figure as the booking flow.

Test Case: Zero and negative weight are refused
Steps: 1. Enter weight 0, then -1, then a very large value.
Expected Result: 0 and negative are refused. A large value either quotes or explains the limit - it never produces NaN.

Test Case: Volumetric weight is applied consistently
Steps: 1. Quote a light but bulky parcel.
Expected Result: The higher of actual and volumetric weight is charged and the UI says which was used.

Preconditions: Signed in as a verified customer
Test Case: Book a pickup shipment end to end
Steps: 1. Open /create. 2. Step 1 sender. 3. Step 2 receiver. 4. Step 3 parcel weight, dimensions and contents. 5. Step 4 pickup, date and payment method. 6. Submit.
Expected Result: The order is created with status pickup_requested. It appears in /orders and on the ops pickups board.

Test Case: Book a drop-off shipment
Steps: 1. As CRT-001 but choose Drop-off at step 4.
Expected Result: The order is created and lands on the ops dropoffs board rather than pickups. No pickup date or agent is demanded.

Test Case: Before the 3PM cutoff today is bookable
Steps: 1. At 14:30 IST open the pickup date picker.
Expected Result: Today is selectable as the earliest pickup date.

Preconditions: Local clock at or after 15:00 IST
Test Case: From the 3PM cutoff the earliest pickup is tomorrow
Steps: 1. At exactly 15:00 IST open the pickup date picker.
Expected Result: Today is no longer selectable and tomorrow is the earliest.
Notes: Covers f23305d. Hub-specific cutoffs override the default

Preconditions: A pincode no pickup agent covers
Test Case: Doorstep pickup is offered only where an agent can reach
Steps: 1. Enter a non-serviceable pickup pincode at step 4.
Expected Result: Pickup is disabled or hidden for that pincode and drop-off is offered instead, with a reason shown.

Test Case: The packaging option is captured
Steps: 1. Choose Pack it for me instead of Already packed. 2. Submit.
Expected Result: packaging_required is set on the order and is visible to ops and to the agent.

Test Case: Each step blocks on incomplete input
Steps: 1. Try to advance each step with required fields blank.
Expected Result: Advance is blocked with per-field messages and the step indicator does not mark the step complete.

Test Case: Pincode lookup fills city and state
Steps: 1. Type a valid 6-digit Indian pincode.
Expected Result: City and state auto-fill. An unknown pincode shows a not-found hint rather than hanging.

Preconditions: The primary postal source is unavailable
Test Case: Pincode lookup falls back to a second source
Steps: 1. Block the primary postal API. 2. Enter a valid pincode.
Expected Result: The second source answers and the field still fills.

Preconditions: Corporate account on an export corridor
Test Case: Bond UT versus IGST selection is captured
Steps: 1. At step 4 choose Bond UT, then IGST.
Expected Result: The selection is stored on the order and surfaces on the docket.

Test Case: Navigating back preserves entered data
Steps: 1. Fill steps 1 to 3. 2. Go back to step 1. 3. Return to step 3.
Expected Result: All entered data is intact with no silent reset.

Preconditions: A signed-in customer whose account KYC is incomplete
Test Case: An unverified account cannot book
Steps: 1. Attempt a booking on an account with missing or flagged documents.
Expected Result: Booking is blocked and the verification banner points at what is missing.

Preconditions: RAZORPAY_KEY_ID and RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET set to test keys
Test Case: Pay now settles the order through Razorpay
Steps: 1. At step 4 choose Pay Now. 2. Complete the Razorpay test payment.
Expected Result: The order payment_status becomes paid and a payments row is written with the gateway reference.

Test Case: A failed gateway payment leaves the order unpaid
Steps: 1. Force a payment failure in the Razorpay test flow.
Expected Result: The order stays pending, an error is shown and retry is offered. No order is marked paid.

Test Case: payment.captured settles an order whose browser died
Steps: 1. Start a pay-now payment. 2. Kill the browser before the callback. 3. Deliver the payment.captured webhook.
Expected Result: The order is settled from the webhook alone.

Test Case: An unsigned webhook delivery is rejected
Steps: 1. POST /api/payments/razorpay/webhook with a bad or missing signature.
Expected Result: Rejected, and no payment row is written.

Test Case: refund.processed is recorded against the order
Steps: 1. Deliver a refund.processed webhook for the payment.
Expected Result: The refund is recorded on the order. The app never issues refunds itself, only records them.

Test Case: Missing gateway keys degrade gracefully
Steps: 1. Unset the Razorpay keys. 2. Open step 4.
Expected Result: The pay-now endpoints return 503 and the other three methods still book. The app does not crash.

Test Case: Pay at pickup is collected by the agent
Steps: 1. Book choosing Pay at pickup. 2. As the agent, collect at pickup.
Expected Result: The order books unpaid. The agent screen shows the amount to collect and settles it on collection.

Test Case: Pay at dropoff is collected at the hub
Steps: 1. Book choosing Pay at dropoff. 2. Settle at the hub.
Expected Result: The amount is shown at drop-off and settles the order when collected.

Test Case: A COD order is flagged as COD across surfaces
Steps: 1. Book with COD. 2. Check /orders, the ops board and the transactions ledger.
Expected Result: COD is identified consistently everywhere.

Preconditions: PAYMENTS_TEST_MODE=1 and signed in as the order owner
Test Case: Test-mode settle marks an order paid with no money moving
Steps: 1. Open a pay-now order. 2. Use the test settle switch beside Pay Now.
Expected Result: A payments row is written with source test_mode and reference test_<order id>. The order is marked paid and the settle is logged.
Notes: Must be unset before the environment takes real payments

Test Case: Test settle cannot settle someone else's order
Steps: 1. As user A, POST /api/payments/test/settle for an order owned by B.
Expected Result: Refused. Only the signed-in owner's own order can be settled.

Test Case: Test settle is unavailable when the flag is off
Steps: 1. POST /api/payments/test/settle.
Expected Result: Refused, and the switch is absent from the UI.

Test Case: The orders list shows the customer's orders
Steps: 1. Open /orders.
Expected Result: Every order for the account is listed with its customer-facing status. Internal-only statuses are not shown raw.

Test Case: Order detail shows the full record
Steps: 1. Open /order/:orderNo.
Expected Result: Sender, receiver, parcel, payment method, payment status and the timeline all render.

Preconditions: A dispatched order with an AWB
Test Case: Tracking by AWB works
Steps: 1. Open /track. 2. Enter the AWB.
Expected Result: The timeline renders with events in order. An unknown AWB gives a not-found state rather than an error page.

Preconditions: An order not yet picked up
Test Case: A cancellation request is raised and reaches ops
Steps: 1. Request cancellation from the order. 2. Open the ops cancellations view as admin.
Expected Result: The request appears as pending for ops to approve or reject.

Test Case: A terminal order cannot be cancelled
Steps: 1. Try to cancel a dispatched order.
Expected Result: The action is unavailable or refused.

Test Case: A customer cannot read another customer's order
Steps: 1. As A, GET /api/orders/:orderNo for an order owned by B.
Expected Result: 404 or 403 with no order data leaked.

Test Case: Order documents are downloadable by their owner only
Steps: 1. As the owner, open the document. 2. As another account, request the same file URL.
Expected Result: The owner gets the file, the other account is refused, and the access is logged.

Test Case: New bookings appear in New jobs automatically
Steps: 1. Book a pickup as a customer. 2. Watch /agent without using a manual refresh path.
Expected Result: The job lands in New jobs on its own.

Preconditions: Free jobs exist for today and for later dates
Test Case: Every free job is visible, with future ones in a Later band
Steps: 1. Open /agent/available.
Expected Result: No free job is hidden. Jobs dated ahead appear under Later.

Test Case: An agent accepts a job
Steps: 1. Accept a job from /agent/available. 2. Open /agent/mine.
Expected Result: The order moves to agent_accepted and appears under the agent's own jobs.

Preconditions: Two agents on the same free job
Test Case: Two agents cannot accept the same job
Steps: 1. Have both agents accept simultaneously.
Expected Result: Exactly one succeeds. The other gets a clear already-taken message.

Test Case: The pickup lifecycle advances correctly
Steps: 1. Mark out for pickup. 2. Mark picked up.
Expected Result: Status moves agent_accepted to out_for_pickup to picked_up, and the customer-facing status updates too.

Test Case: The handover code is required and validated
Steps: 1. Request the handover code on the order. 2. Enter a wrong code. 3. Enter the correct one.
Expected Result: The wrong code is refused inline under the field. The correct code completes the handover.

Preconditions: The agent collected cash on pay-at-pickup jobs
Test Case: The collections screen totals the day correctly
Steps: 1. Open /agent/collections.
Expected Result: The IST day window is used, the total matches the collected orders, and a receipt sheet opens per collection.

Test Case: No toasts are shown on the agent surface
Steps: 1. Perform actions that would toast on the customer app.
Expected Result: No toast appears anywhere under /agent. Feedback is inline on the card or field.

Test Case: An agent cannot reach the customer or ops surfaces
Steps: 1. Navigate to /ops/dashboard and to /home.
Expected Result: Bounced back to the agent surface, and requireRole refuses the ops APIs on the server too.

Test Case: The agent digest and reminders render
Steps: 1. POST /api/internal/wa/agent-schedule?kind=digest. 2. Then the same with ?kind=reminders.
Expected Result: Both render, log the message and write a whatsapp_messages row. Nothing is actually sent while WA_DRY_RUN=1.

Preconditions: Signed in as admin or super_admin
Test Case: The ops dashboard loads with live counts
Steps: 1. Open /ops. 2. Confirm the redirect to /ops/dashboard.
Expected Result: Counts and sections render against real data with no console errors.

Test Case: Each board shows only its own section
Steps: 1. Open /ops/pickups, /ops/dropoffs and /ops/dispatched.
Expected Result: Pickups shows the pickup lane, dropoffs the drop-off lane and dispatched the dispatched orders, with no cross-contamination.

Preconditions: On a board at a desktop viewport
Test Case: The cards and table toggle works on desktop
Steps: 1. Switch from cards to the flat table and back.
Expected Result: Both render the same set and the table carries a stage column.

Preconditions: On a board at a mobile viewport
Test Case: The mobile More menu surfaces Transactions and Users
Steps: 1. Open the More menu on mobile.
Expected Result: Transactions and Users are reachable from it.

Test Case: The default board view is calm - filters are summoned, not always shown
Steps: 1. Open a board fresh.
Expected Result: No filter panel is open by default. A control summons a popover on desktop and a sheet on mobile.

Test Case: The stage filter narrows the board
Steps: 1. Filter by inbound, then hub, then settled, then all.
Expected Result: Only orders whose status maps to the chosen phase remain, and all restores everything.

Test Case: The assignment filter works
Steps: 1. Filter assigned, then unassigned.
Expected Result: Assigned shows only orders with an agent and unassigned only those without.

Preconditions: Orders booked and scheduled across dates
Test Case: Date filters are direction-aware
Steps: 1. On booking date choose today, 7d and 30d. 2. On pickup date choose today, tomorrow and week.
Expected Result: Booking date offers past-facing ranges and pickup date future-facing ones. A range invalid for the field is coerced rather than showing an empty board.

Test Case: The payment method filter works
Steps: 1. Filter by pay_now, pay_at_pickup, pay_at_dropoff and cod.
Expected Result: Each shows only its own method, and COD orders are identified by isCodOrder consistently.

Test Case: Active filters show as removable pills with a count
Steps: 1. Apply three filters. 2. Remove one via its pill. 3. Clear all.
Expected Result: The count matches the number of non-default filters, and removing a pill restores that dimension only.

Preconditions: A board with more orders than the default cap
Test Case: Search is debounced and returns uncapped results
Steps: 1. Type a partial order number or customer name. 2. Watch the network tab.
Expected Result: Requests are debounced rather than one per keystroke, and results are not truncated to the capped default page.
Notes: Covers f2b346e - the two-query capped and filtered split

Test Case: The result count caption is accurate
Steps: 1. Search something with a known number of matches.
Expected Result: The caption states the true total for the filter, not the length of the capped default page.

Test Case: Acting on an order refreshes the filtered view
Steps: 1. With filters applied, assign an agent to an order. 2. Watch the board.
Expected Result: The filtered query key is invalidated and the board reflects the change without a manual reload.

Preconditions: More orders than one PostgREST page, over 1000
Test Case: Order board CSV export is uncapped
Steps: 1. Open a board with more than 1000 matching orders. 2. Export CSV. 3. Count the rows.
Expected Result: The CSV contains every matching order, paged past the ~1000-row PostgREST maximum, and is not truncated.

Test Case: Export respects the active filters
Steps: 1. Apply stage and date filters. 2. Export CSV.
Expected Result: The CSV contains exactly the filtered set, in the same order as the board.

Test Case: Transactions CSV export is uncapped and correct
Steps: 1. Open /ops/transactions. 2. Export CSV.
Expected Result: Every transaction in range is exported, and amounts and dates match the on-screen ledger.

Preconditions: An order with a comma, a quote or a newline in a field
Test Case: CSV escaping is correct
Steps: 1. Create an order whose customer name contains a comma and a double quote. 2. Export and open the file in Sheets.
Expected Result: The row parses into the correct columns with no field bleed.

Preconditions: A pickup order and an active agent
Test Case: An admin assigns a pickup to an agent
Steps: 1. Open the order detail. 2. Pick an agent. 3. Assign.
Expected Result: The order advances automatically and shows the agent name badge, and the agent sees it under their jobs.

Test Case: An inactive agent cannot be assigned
Steps: 1. Try to assign a pickup to an inactive agent.
Expected Result: Refused with a clear message, and only active agents appear in the picker.

Preconditions: Two admins on the same order
Test Case: Concurrent assignment is race-safe
Steps: 1. Have two admins assign different agents at the same instant.
Expected Result: One wins under the shared guard and the other is told the order already moved.

Test Case: Ops order detail shows everything ops needs
Steps: 1. Open /ops/orders/:id.
Expected Result: Customer, sender, receiver, parcel, payment, agent, status history and documents all render, with dates in IST.

Test Case: The verifications queue lists accounts awaiting review
Steps: 1. Open the verifications view. 2. Open one account's documents.
Expected Result: Pending accounts are listed, documents open for review, and each open is logged.

Test Case: The users view lists staff and their roles
Steps: 1. Open /ops/users.
Expected Result: Staff users and roles render, and role changes where offered take effect.

Test Case: Ops approves and rejects cancellations
Steps: 1. Approve one request. 2. Reject another.
Expected Result: The approved order becomes cancelled, the rejected one keeps its status, and the customer sees the outcome.

Test Case: A customer cannot reach the ops console
Steps: 1. Navigate to /ops/dashboard. 2. Call GET /api/ops/orders directly.
Expected Result: Bounced by SurfaceGuard and refused by requireRole on the server.

Test Case: IST and INR formatting are consistent
Steps: 1. Compare dates and amounts across cards, table, detail and CSV.
Expected Result: All dates are IST and all amounts use formatInr, with no UTC drift on the day boundary.
Notes: The startOfIstDayIso dedupe in the merge touches this

Test Case: The today filter uses the IST day, not UTC
Steps: 1. At 00:30 IST filter by today on booking date.
Expected Result: Orders booked after 00:00 IST today are included and yesterday's are not.

Test Case: Sort newest and oldest works
Steps: 1. Toggle the sort.
Expected Result: The order reverses correctly and the export follows the same order.

Preconditions: Signed in with events on an order
Test Case: In-app notifications list with an unread count
Steps: 1. Open /notifications. 2. Read one.
Expected Result: Notifications list newest first and the unread count decreases on read.

Test Case: WhatsApp dry run sends nothing but records everything
Steps: 1. Trigger an order event that notifies.
Expected Result: The message is rendered and logged, a whatsapp_messages row is written, and nothing leaves the server.

Test Case: Unset WhatsApp credentials degrade gracefully
Steps: 1. Trigger a notification with no token set.
Expected Result: The send is skipped and logged, in-app notifications still work, and the login OTP falls back to the server console.

Test Case: Delivery receipts and STOP are handled
Steps: 1. POST a sent, delivered, read and failed receipt to the webhook. 2. POST a STOP message.
Expected Result: Receipts update the message row and STOP opts the number out of further sends.

Test Case: The WhatsApp webhook rejects a wrong secret
Steps: 1. POST /api/whatsapp/webhook/wrong-secret.
Expected Result: Refused. The path segment is the whole authentication.

Test Case: The SMS fallback path is exercised
Steps: 1. Force a WhatsApp OTP failure.
Expected Result: The SMS fallback is attempted and the failure is logged loudly. NOTE: no SMS vendor is wired yet, so expect the logged gap rather than a delivered SMS.

Test Case: Every ops API route requires an ops role
Steps: 1. Call each /api/ops endpoint signed out, then as a customer, then as an agent.
Expected Result: All three are refused. Only admin and super_admin succeed.

Test Case: Every agent API route requires the agent role
Steps: 1. Call /api/agent/pickups/available and /api/agent/pickups/mine as a customer.
Expected Result: Refused.

Preconditions: SESSION_SECRET set to a real random value
Test Case: Session cookies are signed and not forgeable
Steps: 1. Tamper with the session cookie. 2. Reload.
Expected Result: The tampered session is rejected and the user is signed out.

Test Case: SurfaceGuard bounces each role to its own surface
Steps: 1. As an agent open /ops and /home. 2. As an admin open /agent. 3. As a customer open both.
Expected Result: Each is bounced to their own surface. Guarding is cosmetic, so confirm the server also refuses.

Test Case: Identity data is encrypted at rest
Steps: 1. Query account_documents, identity_verifications and kyc_documents directly.
Expected Result: document_no and file_data are ciphertext, not readable values.

Test Case: Document access is logged
Steps: 1. Open a document as ops. 2. Inspect the access log.
Expected Result: Each access is recorded with who and when.

Test Case: Phone change and unlink work
Steps: 1. Change the account phone to a new verified number. 2. Then unlink it.
Expected Result: The new number requires its own OTP and the old number no longer signs in.

Test Case: The serverless build runs
Steps: 1. Deploy the branch to Vercel. 2. Load the app.
Expected Result: The app serves as a serverless function and relative imports resolve with the extension Node needs.

Test Case: Sessions do not break on serverless
Steps: 1. Deploy with no REDIS_URL. 2. Sign in and navigate.
Expected Result: Either sessions persist via the Postgres store or signed cookies, or the gap is explicit. Users must not be signed out at random.

Test Case: Production-honoured bypasses are all off before handover
Steps: 1. Confirm OTP_FIXED_CODE, PAYMENTS_TEST_MODE, IDENTITY_BYPASS and OCR_BYPASS are unset in the customer-facing environment.
Expected Result: All four unset. Each is honoured in production builds, so any one left on is a live hole.

Test Case: Support chat answers and holds a session
Steps: 1. Open the support FAB. 2. Ask a question. 3. Start a new session.
Expected Result: A reply is returned, the session persists across messages, and New session clears it.

Test Case: Support chat is rate limited
Steps: 1. Send many messages rapidly.
Expected Result: The limiter kicks in with a clear message rather than a silent failure.
